qc/runs/kittle-2026-10-09-r2/raw-evidence-index.json (all artifact and source hashes verified as matching)
evidence:
ACHIEVABILITY (pass). Every graded capability is reachable from the seed, the pinned runtime and the public network. (1) Runtime: environment/Dockerfile pins node:22-bookworm-slim with express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 under NODE_PATH. tests/Dockerfile installs the same two packages. tests/test.sh:85-111 chowns /app to 65534 and launches node /app/server.js under env -i with PORT=3000 and DB_PATH=/app/app.db. This matches environment/instructions/integration.md:3-5, which covers Node 22, server.js, 0.0.0.0:3000, NODE_PATH, /app/app.db or DB_PATH, /api/health, import once with no leftover db, and no symlinks. (2) Seed: environment/assets/seed_data.json is byte-identical to solution/app/seed/seed_data.json. It contains every fixture a criterion relies on. K-1 (1 May, 7-day M-11) is expired and has replies K-14 and held K-15. K-10 is at exactly 2026-05-05T11:00:00Z and K-11 is one second later. K-17 is held and overdue. K-2 is held, with earlier version 'Landlords notice recieved.'. K-13 (4 May, 30-day M-13) has earlier version '2,400'. K-16 contains literal <b>/<i>/<u> tags. Dev is walled from M-12. The brief states the 7-day boundary explicitly ('a message sent exactly seven days ago on a seven-day matter is already gone', walls-and-retention.md:23). (3) Measured: qc/repairs/kittle-2026-10-08/results/golden-run.log (sha256 23943bf8... matches the raw-evidence index; all nine matching_source_files hashes match the frozen task) shows a PASS for all 16 functional criteria, gate_constraints and polish_refusal_in_place on the frozen golden, with a real restart. This is scripted Playwright evidence, not a configured judge run, Oracle grade or model score.

TRACEABILITY (pass). I mapped every functional, polish and visual criterion leg to a public sentence. Client scope and signed-out replay: instruction.md:7, walls-and-retention.md:15-17, integration.md:9. Wall routes, links, mentions, live wall and own-wall lift: walls-and-retention.md:17-19 and conversations.md:17,21. Three-level replies with quotes, in send order under the parent: conversations.md:5. Placeholder and expiry boundary: conversations.md:9 and walls-and-retention.md:23-25. Timer shorten, off and partner-only: walls-and-retention.md:23. Hold scope, delete refusal, 'On hold' text and release: walls-and-retention.md:29 and conversations.md:13. Edited mark, staff-only versions, stale-edit refusal that keeps the typed text, author-only edit: conversations.md:9. Formatting, literal markup everywhere and new-tab links: conversations.md:13. Link preview and not-available: conversations.md:17. Per-person unread synced across tabs, new-messages line, mark-unread and deleted not counted: conversations.md:25. Idempotent resend and same-time order across thread, search and transcript: conversations.md:29 and integration.md:7. Live updates that keep the draft, open box and scroll: conversations.md:31. Case-insensitive search, no versions, open at message: walls-and-retention.md:33. Transcript contents: walls-and-retention.md:35. Refusal shown in place: walls-and-retention.md:37. 390 px: conversations.md:33. Timer beside the title: walls-and-retention.md:23. Several criteria avoid ambiguous readings. Unread checks only count Harriet's messages for Dev, plus a relative 'at least 2' for Gwen, so the open question of whether your own messages count is never graded. Version access is checked only for staff (Harriet). Time formats are accepted in 'any clear format' (app_context.md:27). Live waits are 10 s against the brief's 'about five seconds'.

RESIDUAL AMBIGUITIES (all P3, none credible enough to Fail):
(a) Same-time order. conversations.md:29 says 'one consistent order wherever you see them', but sent_once_in_order Part B (functional/judge.toml:215-216) requires send order A,B,C. Second reading: an app that breaks same-timestamp ties by a random UUID is consistent everywhere but not A,B,C. This is weak because the brief says replies go 'in the order they were sent' (conversations.md:5) and integration.md:7 says 'the order stays consistent', and a chat that reorders your own sends is not reasonable. Still, 'send order' appears nowhere for top-level messages.
(b) Symlinks. integration.md:5 says 'don't put symbolic links in /app outside node_modules', which implies links inside node_modules are fine. The template-controlled tests/test.sh:72-83 also exits with 0 reward for a node_modules link whose target is outside /app/node_modules. Plausible case: a builder runs `npm link express`. That conforms to the brief but test.sh refuses to run the app.
(c) Mention name. conversations.md:21 says '@ and a name', and the criteria type '@Dev' (functional/judge.toml:72). An app with no picker that matches only full names ('@Dev Anand') is a second reading. The golden accepts both forms (server.js:208-214).
(d) Delete without replies. The brief never says whether a deleted message that has no replies vanishes or leaves a tombstone. hold_scope_and_release step 1 says 'it disappears'. A WhatsApp-style 'message deleted' tombstone probably still counts, because the text is gone.
(e) Request shape. Replay-based legs assume HTTP requests that can be replayed with fetch (app_context.md:25). The brief states no transport. An app that posts or edits over WebSocket frames, or that copies a link only to the clipboard (the golden also shows it in a visible field, app.js:443-451), is conforming. These are mainly judge-feasibility concerns for other rows.
Workbook note: the Internal Quality Checks row 6 says 'with no network'. The SKILL delivery profile (public network) overrides that, and the brief allows CDN assets (integration.md:3). No defect.
Plausible broken app that could pass this row: none found. Every graded behaviour has a public sentence and a seed fixture.
counterexample: (a) A conforming-by-wording app orders same-timestamp top-level messages by a random UUID tie-breaker. The order is identical in the thread, search and transcript, but B,C,A fails sent_once_in_order Part B. (b) A builder runs `npm link express` in /app. The brief allows symlinks inside node_modules, but test.sh:72-83 exits before launch, so the reward is 0.
suggested_fix: In conversations.md:29, say 'stay in the order they were sent'. In integration.md:5, say no symlinks may point outside /app (including inside node_modules). Optionally add one line that a mention can use a first name.
